title: Incident-report form filling from short case documents

charter.purpose: Expose ways in which a model filling the incident form from a case document fails to meet the stated instructions, and route each failure to the loci that could be at fault.
charter.output: Per-model observation and run records with plural verdicts and live loci, plus an unranked report for human triage.
scope_in: Short English case documents rendered as prose, a two-column table, or an email.
Australian phone numbers and dates written in words or day-first numerals.
The nine declared fields of the incident form.
scope_out: Any claim that a model understands incidents, safety, or forms in general.
Ranking models, scoring them, or declaring any model fit for use.
Documents in other languages, scanned images, or multi-incident reports.

negations.replacement_sentence: `incident_date` is the date of the incident written as DD/MM/YYYY.
`phone` is the reporter's contact number in Australian national format with a leading 0 and spaces: 04XX XXX XXX for mobiles or 0X XXXX XXXX for landlines.

ambiguity.question: When the document writes a date as two numeric fields NN/NN/YYYY, which field is the day?

rivals.label: day_first
rivals.instruction: Read numeric dates of the form NN/NN/YYYY as DD/MM/YYYY (Australian convention).

rivals.label: month_first
rivals.instruction: Read numeric dates of the form NN/NN/YYYY as MM/DD/YYYY (United States convention).
